You are working in an isolated git worktree of the DeepSeek Harness monorepo. FIRST, make sure you start from the current head of `claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt`, commit `2cf413ec3`: run `git log --oneline -1`; if your worktree is older, run `git merge --ff-only 2cf413ec3`, confirm, then `pnpm install --offline`. Do not work on an older base.

Read CLAUDE.md, packages/AGENTS.md, examples/AGENTS.md, docs/AGENTS.md, docs/testing.md, docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md, and follow every convention (everything is a plugin; registrations are effects; per-file 100% coverage; bilingual triplets; model-visible ⟺ logged; every package owns `./invariant`; a product-visible plugin needs a Loader-booted e2e).

## Task: rollout slices 4 and 5 of the composition-manifest note

The design is `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-composition-manifest.md`; read it whole. Slices 1 to 3 are landed: study `packages/components/components` (digests, layers), the three adapters `components-tools`, `components-prompt`, `components-presets`, and `components-manifest` (the `composition/manifest` writer with log-derived deduplication and its fixture `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest/`). Then read the seams slices 4 and 5 observe: `packages/skill/*` (the skill provider registry, the local implementation, the `skill` tool and `SkillInvocationSource`), `packages/extensions/cordis-host-runner` (the dynamic package runner and the `cordis/*` event family; note `scripts/rescope-vendor.ts` carries an allowlist for the self-referential `cordis/*` events, which a new `cordis/dynamic-changed` event may need), and `ctx.loader.entries()` in the vendored loader. Do NOT touch `packages/verification/**`, `packages/improvement/**`, `packages/guard/**`, or `scripts/verify-village-composition.ts` (other agents own them); read them only. Implement exactly slices 4 and 5 and nothing from slices 6 and 7:

1. **Slice 4, skill generations**: `skillDigest()` in `dsh-skill` (the canonical value the note specifies for a skill body and metadata), the `digest` field on the `skill` tool's canonical value and on `SkillInvocationSource` so a session log records which generation of a skill a turn invoked, `dsh-components-skills` under `packages/components/` registering one descriptor per skill at the producer's layer and following the skill registry's change event, and the mutation fixture the note names (a skill edited in place yields a new address, the old one leaves the registry, the next manifest differs). Unit coverage; keyless snapshot re-recorded only if a model-visible or user-visible rendering changed (check `examples/*/tests/snapshots` for skill scenarios and follow `tests/headless.snapshot.ts`).
2. **Slice 5, dynamic packages**: `cordis/dynamic-changed` on `dsh-cordis-host-runner` (declared with the event JSDoc the catalog requires, allowlisted in `scripts/rescope-vendor.ts` if the rescope gate needs it), `dsh-components-packages` over `ctx.loader.entries()` and the dynamic runner registering a `plugin` descriptor per composed entry with the canonical value the note specifies (`registration` basis) and `provenance: 'synthesized'` for a dynamically mounted package, and the quarantine fixture: a session that mounts a dynamic package mid-run has a manifest whose entries mark it, proven in a Loader-booted e2e under `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-quarantine/`.
3. Docs: README pairs of every touched package, `docs/subsystems/components.md` (+ ZH) extended with type-equiv blocks in sync, catalogs regenerated (`pnpm run gen-cordis-catalog`, `gen-config-catalog` if a Config changed, `gen-doc-graphs`, `gen-persistence-catalog` if a session event changed) with Chinese twins mirrored by hand and pairing re-recorded, and the note's Rollout marking slices 4 and 5 landed with deviations recorded in its Proposal (EN + ZH, pairing re-recorded). Register new packages and fixtures in `examples/package.json`, root `tsconfig.json` references, the components aggregate tsconfig, `knip.json`, `scripts/type-equiv.manifest.json`, and the README model-experience gate as the sibling packages are.

Gates before committing, all must pass: `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `vitest run --coverage --coverage.include='packages/components/*/src/**' --coverage.include='packages/skill/*/src/**' --coverage.include='packages/extensions/cordis-host-runner/src/**' packages/components packages/skill packages/extensions/cordis-host-runner`, `vitest run --config vitest.e2e.config.ts packages/components packages/skill`, `pnpm run rescope-vendor:check`, `pnpm run verify-package-invariants`, `pnpm run verify-cordis-config`, `pnpm run knip`, `pnpm run doc-sync`.

Constraints: never commit credentials; `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is absent. Put no model name or identifier in code, docs, or the commit message. Commit on your worktree branch with the message `feat(components): skill generations and dynamic-package descriptors in the manifest` ending with these two trailer lines exactly:

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HEXjzxR7CyMizem5kFAB4C

Report back: the commit sha and branch, the canonical values as implemented, every deviation from the note, the gate commands with results, and anything you could not do.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- dsh-archive-agent-notes: Use when adding, auditing, pruning, archiving, restoring, or reviewing Agent Notes in deepseek-harness; checks every new note for superseded active records, classifies implemented notes by future decision value, deletes rejected notes that no longer prevent a tempting fallacy, and applies the frozen archived/{kind} triplet and manifest rules.
- dsh-code-review: Use when reviewing a pull request in the deepseek-harness repo — orients the reviewer to this codebase's standards (AGENTS.md conventions, defensive patterns, ADRs, quality gates) and the review-specific checks that code alone can't show
- dsh-doc-site-sync: Use when publishing, updating, moving, or removing DeepSeek Harness documentation website pages; editing website/docs.ts mappings or navigation; diagnosing a page missing from the VitePress site; fixing projected documentation links; or running the docs:dev, docs:check, and doc-sync workflow after website-content changes.
- dsh-doc-standards: Use when writing, moving, reviewing, or auditing documentation in the deepseek-harness repo — choosing hierarchy and detail, separating tutorials from references, checking tutorial progression, trimming doc slop, responding to a verify-doc-budgets failure, or requests like "improve the docs", "audit the docs", "where should this be documented", or "this doc is too long".
- dsh-find-simplifications: Use when working in the deepseek-harness repo to find non-obvious simplification candidates, write proposed Agent Notes or inline TODO/FIXME/XXX notes, audit or coalesce superseded Agent Notes, or fold worthwhile simplification ideas from another PR; especially for dead, duplicated, speculative, over-built, added-then-removed, or hand-rolled-where-a-dependency-exists surfaces.
- dsh-merging-stacked-prs: Use when landing a stack of dependent GitHub PRs (A ← B ← C, where each bases on the one below) onto master, merging a PR whose base is another open PR's branch, or whenever a request mentions "stacked PRs", "PR stack", "dependent PRs", or merging several related PRs in sequence. Requires every same-repository dependency chain to use GitHub's official stacked-PR feature before landing so GitHub owns stack-wide rules, CI, ordering, retargeting, and merge state.
- dsh-pre-push-checks: Use before pushing, force-pushing, marking ready for review, or claiming checks pass on a deepseek-harness branch, and immediately after gh stack sync publishes rewritten branches, to select the smallest tests and checks that cover the outgoing or just-published diff without reflexively running the full repository suite.
- dsh-prose-standard: Use when writing, reviewing, restoring, trimming, or auditing prose in the deepseek-harness repo, including deciding where documentation or comments are required across Markdown, JSDoc, code and test comments, prompts, descriptions, diagnostics, and CLI or UI strings.
- dsh-trim-cot-leakage: Use when auditing or fixing prose that reads like a leaked reasoning transcript — dead design-session citations such as (decision N), audit item codes, or §N of uncommitted drafts; change narration such as "used to", "no longer", "this cut"; stack or review vantage ("a later PR in this stack", "rejected in review"); reviewer-addressed justifications; control-flow narration; or hedged planning residue in comments, JSDoc, docs, or Agent Notes.
- record-browser-gif: Record browser or Web UI interaction demos as optimized GIFs using the available built-in browser, state-based frame capture, and deterministic encoding, then publish to a dedicated assets branch when the task includes attaching the GIF to a pull request. Use when asked to make, record, or generate a GIF that demonstrates a browser workflow, and for every pull request that changes product-user-visible GUI behavior, which MUST include a GIF recorded from the pull request's real server and model flow.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers a dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- mcp-builder: Guide for creating high-quality MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that enable LLMs to interact with external services through well-designed tools. Use when building MCP servers to integrate external APIs or services, whether in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript (MCP SDK).
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. # AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` with no compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities
python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and safe residue from deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns this signal
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When required `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; do not merge before checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, and real-API e2e for provider behavior.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or for an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).

---STATUS---

1	# Agent Note: Content-addressed identity and the composition manifest event
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-composition-manifest.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	Every identity in the harness names a slot rather than the bytes in it. A `ComponentId` is "derived from its kind and the owning seam's stable name, never from mount order" ([`dsh-components`](../../../../packages/components/components/README.md)), a skill is addressed by its kebab-case name, a prompt section and a tool by their registered names, a preset by its directory name, and a plugin by its package name. Editing a skill body in place leaves all of those addresses unchanged, so a leaderboard cannot separate the generation before the edit from the generation after it, a rollback has no earlier address to return to, and a decontamination check has nothing to key on — the failure the [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) records under its rejected "single mutable knowledge store" alternative and forbids in principle P5.
10	
11	Nothing durable records which components a session had in play. The `request/header` event carries each epoch's assembled system prompt text and tool schemas, which is enough to replay a request and not enough to name what produced it: it carries no component identity, provenance, lineage, or registry layer; a skill body loaded through the `skill` tool reaches the transcript as a tool result and never the header; and a dynamic package mounted through [`tool-cordis`](../../../../packages/extensions/tool-cordis/README.md) that registers no tool is invisible in it. The component registry itself is composition-time state that dies with the process, as [the component-registry seam note](2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) states outright.
12	
13	Four consumers are blocked on that gap. [`dsh-scorekeeper`](../../../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md) ships no `composition_hash`, `component_ids`, or `skills_used` field because no event supplies one. W4 stage 1's invariant — a skill result whose digest is absent from the manifest fails — has no manifest to check against. The trajectory exporter can withhold a held-out environment but cannot tell a curated composition from one an agent mutated mid-session, so a synthesized skill body can reach a training set unannounced. And W4 stage 9's knowledge ledger has no address to mirror its entries against, which is what makes "a ledger entry with no matching manifest occurrence never counts as having been in play" enforceable rather than aspirational.
14	
15	## Proposal
16	
17	**One digest function, one address form.** [`dsh-components`](../../../../packages/components/components/README.md) gains `ComponentDigest` (a `Branded<'ComponentDigest'>` from `dsh-brand`) and two pure functions: `componentDigest(kind, canonical)` returns the lowercase SHA-256 hex of `` `${kind}\n${JSON.stringify(canonical)}` ``, and `componentAddress(id, digest)` returns `` `${id}@${digest}` ``. The kind is inside the hashed bytes so two kinds whose canonical values coincide never share an address. The digest is the full 64 hex characters everywhere it is stored or compared, matching `environmentContentHashes` in [`dsh-environments`](../../../../packages/improvement/environments/README.md); truncating it for a card or a table is a presentation choice that never enters a log or the ledger. `ComponentDescriptor` gains a required `digest: ComponentDigest` and a required `digestBasis: 'content' | 'registration'`. As landed, `canonical` is typed `ComponentCanonical` — a JSON value — so a producer cannot hand the hash a value `JSON.stringify` would drop, and `componentAddress` returns a plain string: an address is minted and compared, never received across a boundary that a brand would guard.
18	
19	**Each producer owns its canonical value.** The registry ships no per-kind canonicalization for the same reason it ships no kind: each producer declares its `ComponentKindMap` member by declaration merging and exports the pure function that canonicalizes it, so a kind added later needs no change in the registry or in the manifest writer. The table below fixes the canonical value of every kind this note introduces. As landed, the exported function is the kind's digest rather than its bare canonical value — `agentProviderDigest(provider)`, and `skillDigest(definition)` as the skill row already names — so a consumer recomputing an address calls the producer instead of rebuilding the canonical value from the table.
20	
21	**The registry becomes layered.** `ComponentRegistry` was one flat `Map`, so it could not answer "what does this agent see". It uses `ScopedLayers` from `dsh-scope`, exactly as [`ctx.tools`](../../../../packages/core/tools/README.md) and [`ctx.skills`](../../../../packages/skill/skill/README.md) already do: `register()` files into the calling context's scope, and `list({ kind, scope })` merges the global layer with the viewing scope's chain, the nearest layer's entry winning a duplicate id. A descriptor read back through a scope carries `layer: 'global' | 'agent'` — `global` when the winning registration sits in the global layer, `agent` when it sits in a layer of that agent's scope chain. A deeper chain still reads as `agent`, because a subagent writes its own manifest into its own session. Ids are unique per layer, so a duplicate in one layer still throws `COMPONENT_DUPLICATE_ID` while the same id in a different layer shadows.
22	
23	The derived `layer` rides `ComponentView`, a distinct read type extending `ComponentDescriptor`, rather than an optional descriptor field: a producer registers a descriptor and cannot assert its own layer, and a reader always has one. `get(id, { scope })` takes the same viewing scope as `list({ kind, scope })`, the `SkillViewOptions` pattern `dsh-skill` already uses for its two reads. The registry publishes no change notification — the rejected `components/change` alternative below is why — so the `ScopedLayers` change callback is an explained no-op.
24	
25	**The manifest writer reads one registry.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-manifest` at `packages/components/components-manifest/` injects `agents` and `components` and nothing else. On `agent/pre-step` it calls `next()` first, recomputes `ctx.components.list({ scope: agent })` for the calling agent, compares the resulting `compositionSha256` with the last `composition/manifest` event in that session's log, and appends a new event through `agent.session.append()` only when the two differ — the shape [`dsh-budget-policy`](../../../../packages/guard/budget-policy/README.md) already uses to fold and append before a step opens. Recomputing rather than tracking incrementally is what keeps it correct across HMR disposal, a preset mounted after creation, and scope shadowing: the writer holds no subscription state that any of those three orderings could invalidate.
26	
27	**Every other seam reaches the manifest through an adapter.** The one-adapter-per-seam rule [the component-registry note](2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) established is what keeps the writer from reading registries it does not own, and each adapter follows its seam's own change notification: `dsh-components-tools` follows `tools/change`, `dsh-components-prompt` follows `system-prompt/change`, `dsh-components-skills` follows `tools/result` for the `skill` tool, `dsh-components-presets` follows the `agent-preset/selected` Cordis event, and the shipped `dsh-components-subagents` already follows `subagent/provider-added` and `subagent/provider-removed`. One seam emits nothing today: the dynamic Cordis runner behind `tool-cordis` reports no change when a package is defined, run, stopped, or removed, so `dsh-cordis-host-runner` gains an unfiltered `cordis/dynamic-changed(agent, pluginId)` Cordis event — `@mode emit`, not scope-filtered, so no scope-scan metadata applies — and `dsh-components-packages` follows it.
28	
29	**A skill is in play once its body is loaded, not once it is listed.** `ctx.skills.list()` returns summaries without bodies, so registering every discoverable skill would need a body load per catalog entry per step and would still address a summary rather than the knowledge. `dsh-skill` therefore exports `skillDigest(definition)` over the loaded definition, the `skill` tool's canonical output value gains a `digest` field (absent from `renderSkillContent`, so the model-facing text is unchanged, and durable in `tool/result`), and `SkillInvocationSource` gains the same field so the user-explicit `/name` injection records it too. `dsh-components-skills` registers a `skill` component from either durable record through `exec.agent.ctx`, never by re-parsing the rendered `<skill_content>` block. Skills that were reachable but never loaded stay out of the manifest; the catalog they came from is already durable as the `skill-catalog` message source.
30	
31	**What slices 2 and 3 landed differently.** Five deviations, each the smallest the code admitted. The `tool` canonical value carries no output schema: `ToolSchema` — what `ctx.tools.schemas(scope)` projects and what the model receives — is name, description, and parameter schema, and the canonical output declaration is never model-visible, so addressing it would need the registry to project it beside the wire schema. The `prompt-section` adapter needs a registration read the prompt registry did not expose, so `SystemPrompt` gains `sections(scope?)`, the merged registrations in assembly order with each `text` as it stands. The `preset` adapter needs the trust, the composition path, and the resolved rows of a mount, none of which `PresetMount` carried, so `dsh-agent-presets` records `trust`, `path`, and `tree` on it; a row whose `config` does not survive the lossless-JSON boundary contributes `null`, exactly as an absent one does. That adapter also reconciles on `agent/created` beside `agent-preset/selected`, because a session that starts on the deployment default commits no selection event and the roster publishes no mount notification — `livePresetMounts()` reports a torn-down mount by pruning it, so reconciling against that reading is what removal is. And a `user`-trust preset is recorded with `provenance: 'synthesized'`: the roster records the root a preset was discovered under, never its author, and a locally authored composition carries the same trust as shell access.
32	
33	**The manifest payload landed narrower than this note states.** It carries `version`, `components`, and `compositionSha256` alone. `reason` names values only slices 4 and 5 can produce, `dynamicPackagesMounted` and `synthesized` summarize kinds slice 5 introduces, and `presetId` would make the writer read a registry it does not own — the writer injects `agents` and `components` and nothing else, and a consumer that needs the preset in play reads the `preset` entry in `components`. Each field arrives with the slice that produces its input.
34	
35	## What each kind hashes
36	
37	| Kind | Canonical value | Basis | Producer |
38	|---|---|---|---|
39	| `skill` | `[name, description, whenToUse ?? null, invocation.modelInvocable, invocation.userInvocable, metadata ?? null, content]` from the loaded `SkillDefinition` | content | `dsh-components-skills`, over `skillDigest()` in `dsh-skill` |
40	| `prompt-section` | `[name, order, complete === true, text]` when `PromptSection.text` is a string; `[name, order, complete === true, null]` when it is a provider evaluated per assembly | content, else registration | `dsh-components-prompt` |
41	| `tool` | the model-facing `ToolSchema` as `ctx.tools.schemas(agent)` projects it: name, description, parameter schema, output schema, in the registry's own field order | content | `dsh-components-tools` |
42	| `preset` | `[id, trust, rows]`, where `rows` is the preset's composition after `include` resolution as `[id, name, config, disabled]` per row, with every `name` that resolves to a path rewritten relative to the preset directory | content | `dsh-components-presets` |
43	| `plugin` | `[packageName, version, patchLayerSha256]`, the version from the resolved package manifest and `patchLayerSha256` the SHA-256 over the ordered `cordis.patch.yml` rows of the bundles in force | content | `dsh-components-packages`, over `ctx.loader.entries()` |
44	| `dynamic-package` | `[pluginId, packageId, hostSource, clientSource]` from `ctx.dynamicCordisRunner.inspectPlugin(agent, pluginId)` | content | `dsh-components-packages` |
45	| `agent-provider` | `[provider]` | registration | `dsh-components-subagents` |
46	
47	A digest never covers the viewing scope, the working directory, a wall-clock time, an absolute path (`SkillDefinition.path`, `SkillResourceBase`'s directory, `AgentPreset.path`), a discovery `source` or `rank`, a provider name, or any value a registry computes per assembly. Two hosts that discovered the same skill under different roots, and the same body re-registered through a different provider, therefore address identically; one byte changed in a skill body, a tool parameter description, a static prompt section, or a preset row moves the digest. A `registration`-basis digest addresses the registration and not the bytes the model saw, which is the honest statement for a section whose text is a function of the assembly; the rendered bytes stay where they already are, in `request/header`.
48	
49	## The `composition/manifest` event
50	
51	`dsh-components-manifest` declaration-merges one member into `SessionEventMap` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types`. It is **log-only** and carries no `@mode` tag: a session log event has no dispatch mode, it rides the single `session/event` emit, and `gen-persistence-catalog` rejects the tag outright — the repo's `@mode` and payload-`@param` rules govern the Cordis bus event this note adds, not this one. It is **required-on-read**, without the envelope's `ignorable: true` marker, because every consumer below keys a refusal on it: a build that cannot interpret the type would otherwise fold a scoreboard row and write an export line for a session it cannot prove was unquarantined ([the version mechanism](../../implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)). Its payload fields, each carrying its own JSDoc so [the generated catalog](../../../../docs/persistence-catalog.md) documents them:
52	
53	- `kind: 'composition/manifest'` and `version: 1`, the self-declared payload version the environment stamp also carries.
54	- `reason`: why this manifest was written — `'session-start'`, `'preset-mounted'`, `'skill-loaded'`, `'tools-changed'`, `'prompt-changed'`, or `'package-mounted'`, decided by which kinds changed since the previous manifest.
55	- `presetId`: the preset the agent runs, resolved through `resolveSessionPreset()`; absent when the deployment composes none.
56	- `components`: one entry per component in play, ordered by `id`, each `{ id, digest, kind, provenance, lineage?, layer, digestBasis }`.
57	- `compositionSha256`: SHA-256 over the ordered `id@digest` addresses joined by newlines — the deduplication key and the `composition_hash` the scoreboard row wants.
58	- `dynamicPackagesMounted`: whether any entry has kind `dynamic-package`.
59	- `synthesized`: the ids of every entry whose `provenance` is `synthesized`, in the same order.
60	
61	The four-goal note's sketch lists a `seq` field; the envelope already carries `seq`, so the payload does not repeat it. The first manifest is appended before the session's first `request/header`, because `agent/pre-step` runs before the step assembles its request and the preset has already settled by then — a preset chosen after creation commits `agent-preset/selected` while the session is still blank. Every later change to the set in play produces the next differing manifest at the next step, which is the first step whose model request that change can reach.
62	
63	## Quarantine
64	
65	A session is quarantined when its latest manifest reports `dynamicPackagesMounted` or a non-empty `synthesized`, and equally when its log carries no manifest at all: a session that cannot prove what was in play is exactly as unusable as one that mounted code an agent wrote. `SessionFacts.identity` in [`dsh-scorekeeper`](../../../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md) gains a `composition` group folded from the latest manifest — `compositionSha256`, the entry count, `presetId`, `dynamicPackagesMounted`, and `synthesized` — plus `skillsUsed`, the `id@digest` addresses of every `skill` entry any manifest of the session named. Its `./invariant` companion gains one relation beside the three it checks today: for every `tool/result` of the `skill` tool carrying a digest, some `composition/manifest` at or before that event's `seq` names a `skill` component with that digest, and a result whose digest appears in no manifest is reported as a record disagreeing with its own log. [`dsh-trajectories`](../../../../packages/improvement/trajectories/README.md) gains `includeQuarantined?: boolean` on `TrajectoryExportRequest` and a `quarantined` count on `TrajectoryExportReport`, symmetric with `includeHeldOut` and `heldOut`: absent, the export refuses every quarantined session and accounts for it in the count rather than dropping it silently. The complementary quarantine — a Harness Engineer proposal that touches an evaluator-owned path — belongs to W1 stage 7 and stays there.
66	
67	## The knowledge ledger
68	
69	`@deepseek-ai/dsh-archive` at `packages/improvement/archive/` (`ctx.archive`) holds the cross-session records over [`ctx.storage.domain`](../../../../packages/storage/storage-domain/README.md), through a `defineDomain` spec whose record schemas are zod, routed to whichever backend the deployment configures. Two tables: `variants`, keyed by the `HarnessVariant` id (base commit plus patch-set hash) with the fields the four-goal note fixes — `parent`, `operator`, `patch`, `scores`, `evaluations[]`, `children[]`, `status`, `proposer`; and `generations`, keyed by `id@digest` with `componentId`, `digest`, `kind`, `provenance`, `lineage` (the parent's address, absent for a root), `evidenceSessions[]`, `results`, and `status`. A mutation mints a new row rather than rewriting one, so a generation's bytes and its address never diverge.
70	
71	`status` is `alive`, `dominated`, `promoted`, or `deprecated`. `alive` is evaluated or newly minted and still eligible for parent sampling; `dominated` lost to another generation of its lineage on every measured cell and stays sampleable and auditable, never deleted, which is the archive semantics the four-goal note's rejected best-only alternative exists to preserve; `promoted` carries the `PromotionDecision` that moved it into curated source; `deprecated` is what the department scoreboard writes once a paired present-versus-absent delta has stayed at or below zero over the configured number of runs. Lineage is stored on both ends — `lineage` on the child for the auditor walking up, `children[]` on the parent for the sampler's `1/(1+children)` weight — and a status change appends a revision rather than removing a row.
72	
73	The ledger's `./invariant` companion owns the manifest-versus-ledger relation, an assertion over mutable data against the authoritative event stream the [package invariant rules](../../../../packages/AGENTS.md) require: for every generation row, each session named in `evidenceSessions` must carry a `composition/manifest` whose `components` hold that exact `id@digest`. A row that names an evidence session with no matching occurrence is reported and never counts as having been in play, so a promotion cannot rest on a session the component was not actually composed into.
74	
75	## Alternatives considered
76	
77	**Derive the manifest from `request/header`.** The header already records the assembled system prompt and every tool schema of each epoch, so a fold over it would need no new event. It is rejected because the header carries rendered text and no identity: provenance, lineage, and layer are absent, a loaded skill body never reaches it, and a dynamic package that registers no tool leaves it unchanged — precisely the three cases the quarantine has to catch.
78	
79	**Keep the registry composition-time only, with no session event.** `ctx.components` is already the inventory, so a consumer could read it live. It is rejected because every consumer here reads persisted logs after the fact — the scorekeeper folds them, the exporter writes from them, the ledger invariant checks against them — and composition-time truth dies with the process.
80	
81	**One manifest per session, written at creation.** A single record would be smaller and simpler to fold. It is rejected because a skill load, a preset switch, and a dynamic mount all change the set mid-session, and a start-of-session record would report a clean composition for exactly the sessions the quarantine exists to flag.
82	
83	**Hash each component's rendered contribution.** Hashing what the model actually received would tie the digest to the bytes in the transcript. It is rejected because rendering depends on the working directory, the wall clock, and the viewing scope, so two identical compositions on two hosts would address differently and decontamination would key on noise; `request/header` already owns the rendered bytes, and the manifest owns identity.
84	
85	**Put the per-kind canonicalization in the manifest writer.** One switch over kinds inside the writer would avoid an adapter per seam. It is rejected because the writer would then have to know every kind, which is the coupling `ComponentKindMap`'s declaration merging removes, and a kind added downstream could not be digested at all.
86	
87	**A monotonic version counter per component instead of a content address.** A `skill@3` label is shorter and human-readable. It is rejected for the reason the four-goal note's "single mutable knowledge store" alternative was: a counter is authored rather than derived, so two hosts that refine the same body disagree on the number, a body restored from an ancestor gets a new number instead of its old address, and no consumer can verify the label against the bytes.
88	
89	**A `components/change` event with an incremental writer.** Mirroring `tools/change` would let the writer maintain the manifest between steps instead of recomputing it. It is rejected because recomputation is one registry read and one hash per step and cannot be wrong, while an incremental writer would have to stay correct across HMR disposal, preset remounts, and scope shadowing; no consumer in this note needs a change notification, so the event is not added until one does.
90	
91	**The ledger as session events rather than storage.** Recording generations in the log would keep everything on one plane. It is rejected because a ledger spans sessions and outlives every one of them, and because the manifest-versus-ledger invariant needs two planes to be a real check: an entry that is itself a session event could not be contradicted by the session events it cites.
92	
93	## Acceptance criteria
94	
95	- A Loader-booted composition at `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest/` appends one `composition/manifest` before the session's first `request/header`; the event names the preset id, carries one entry per component in play with a `digest`, `provenance`, `layer`, and `digestBasis`, and its `compositionSha256` equals a recomputation from the ordered `id@digest` addresses in the persisted log.
96	- In the same fixture, the agent calls the `skill` tool once; a second manifest follows with `reason: 'skill-loaded'`, one added `skill` entry whose digest equals `skillDigest()` over that body, and a different `compositionSha256`. A step that changes nothing appends no third event.
97	- Two runs of that fixture under different temporary workspace roots and different `DSH_HOME` values produce byte-identical `compositionSha256` values, proving absolute paths, discovery roots, and timestamps are outside every digest.
98	- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest-mutation/` runs the same composition twice with one byte of the skill body changed between the runs; exactly one entry's digest differs, `compositionSha256` differs, and every other entry is unchanged.
99	- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest-quarantine/` composes `tool-cordis`, defines and runs a dynamic package, and proves the next manifest reports `dynamicPackagesMounted: true` with the package's id in `synthesized`; the trajectory export then withholds that session and counts it as `quarantined`, and the same export with `includeQuarantined` writes it.
100	- A keyless unit test over a synthetic log proves the scorekeeper invariant reports a `skill` tool result whose digest appears in no preceding manifest, and accepts the same result once a manifest names it; a second proves a session with no manifest at all folds to a quarantined record rather than a clean one.
101	- A keyless unit test in `packages/improvement/archive/tests/` proves the ledger invariant reports a generation row whose evidence session carries no manifest occurrence of its `id@digest`, and accepts the row once one exists.
102	- The persisted-log snapshot suite `examples/headless-agent` owns records the manifest events for the scenario that composes the manifest writer; the event is log-only and changes no model-visible text, so the required coverage is the persisted log rather than a transcript re-record ([testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md)).
103	
104	## Rollout
105	
106	1. **Landed.** `dsh-components`: the `ComponentDigest` brand, `componentDigest()` and `componentAddress()`, the required `digest` and `digestBasis` on `ComponentDescriptor`, and the `ScopedLayers` layering with `list({ kind, scope })` and the derived `layer`. Updates `dsh-components-subagents` (the `agent-provider` canonical value `[provider]`, basis `registration`) and `dsh-command-components` (the invoking agent becomes the viewing scope; its rendered line still names no digest or layer, because no runnable example composes `/components` and a rendering change owes a keyless snapshot), [`docs/subsystems/components.md`](../../../../docs/subsystems/components.md), and the three package READMEs.
107	2. **Landed.** The composition-time adapters and their canonical values: `dsh-components-tools`, `dsh-components-prompt`, and `dsh-components-presets` at `packages/components/`, each following its seam's existing change event. Adds `SystemPrompt.sections(scope?)` and the `trust`, `path`, and `tree` fields on `PresetMount`.
108	3. **Landed.** `dsh-components-manifest`: the `composition/manifest` declaration, the `agent/pre-step` writer with `compositionSha256` deduplication, the regenerated `known-event-types.ts` and persistence catalog, the invariant companion over consecutive manifests and their addresses, and the `composition-manifest` fixture.
109	4. Skill generations: `skillDigest()` in `dsh-skill`, the `digest` field on the `skill` tool's canonical value and on `SkillInvocationSource`, `dsh-components-skills`, and the mutation fixture.
110	5. Dynamic packages: `cordis/dynamic-changed` on `dsh-cordis-host-runner`, `dsh-components-packages` over `ctx.loader.entries()` and the dynamic runner, and the quarantine fixture.
111	6. Quarantine consumers: the `composition` group and `skillsUsed` on `SessionFacts`, the scorekeeper invariant relation, and `includeQuarantined` with the `quarantined` count in `dsh-trajectories`.
112	7. `dsh-archive`: the domain spec, the `variants` and `generations` tables, the four statuses and their transitions, the two-ended lineage edges, and the manifest-versus-ledger invariant.
113	
114	## Risks
115	
116	A `registration`-basis digest cannot detect a change in what a provider-evaluated prompt section produced, so two runs whose dynamic sections differed share an address. `request/header` carries those bytes and a comparison that needs them must read it; a leaderboard keyed on the manifest alone will pool the two.
117	
118	A `plugin` digest keys on package name and version, and every workspace package here is `0.0.1`, so a source edit does not move it. `HarnessVariant`'s base commit plus patch-set hash is what addresses harness source, and a comparison that keys on plugin digests alone will pool generations of the same package.
119	
120	The manifest names components, not their transitive effects. An MCP server whose remote tool descriptions change without a re-registration, or a skill whose body references a file that changed, keeps its digest; only what the canonical value covers is addressed.
121	
122	Required-on-read means a build that does not know `composition/manifest` refuses a log containing it. That is the intended trade — the alternative is a build silently treating a quarantined session as clean — and it is affordable only under the pre-release stance in the root [AGENTS.md](../../../../AGENTS.md).
123	
124	A composition that churns its visible tool set every step writes one manifest per step. Deduplication by `compositionSha256` keeps a stable composition to exactly one event, and a churning one is paying for a real change in what the model can call, but a scoped restriction toggled per step would inflate a log with events no consumer distinguishes.
125

## alphaXiv
alphaXiv provides access to a database of over 2.5 million academic research papers from arXiv. (computer science, mathematics, physics, statistics, quantitative biology/finance, electrical engineering, NOT biomedical, clinical, or life science papers from PubMed, Cell, Nature) These tools are useful when the user asks about, references, or discusses academic papers, scientific research, scholarly literature, citations, research topics, or anything related to academic work. If the user mentions a research area, methodology, scientific concept, asks for literature reviews, wants to find related work, or asks questions that could benefit from academic sources, consider using the search tools. When the user references a specific paper or asks about its content, the paper content and PDF query tools can help. Prefer searching for and citing real papers over relying on memory alone for research questions. The library tools manage the user's own folders of bookmarked papers: a paper can live in several folders at once, and 'to read', 'reading', and 'completed' are just the default folders rather than exclusive states. The researcher tools answer questions about people: who works on a subject, an organization's roster, where someone is now, who they publish with, and the user's own follows. Results address papers as [ID=<id>] and researchers as [SLUG=<slug>]; pass those values back to the tools that take a paper id or a researcher slug, and render them as https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/<id> and https://www.alphaxiv.org/@<slug> rather than showing the bracketed handle to the user.

## Anthropic_Economic_Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

## Firecrawl
Firecrawl provides web, developer, and research search. Use firecrawl_search to find relevant results across the web and specialized indexes. For a programming question, firecrawl_developer_search searches indexed repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and curated documentation sites and returns the matched passages, and skills: "only" narrows it to agent-skill files; firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"] reaches the same index beside ordinary web results, returning the hits in the web group rather than as passages and offering no skills filter. For a biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature question, the firecrawl_research_* tools search the paper index, while categories: ["research"] on firecrawl_search filters ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites. Use the firecrawl_research_* tools to search academic and research literature, expand from anchor papers via the citation graph, and read full-text passages from a specific paper. All tools are read-only and return ranked results.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Hugging_Face
Hugging Face Hub MCP server for models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, and docs.
Prefer this connector's live Hub capabilities over the public website for all configured listings such as today's trending models, the current model leaderboard, daily papers, and paper popularity.

Use hf_fs for Hub filesystem and discovery:
- trending models: ls hf://models/trending
- trending datasets or Spaces: ls hf://datasets/trending, ls hf://spaces/trending
- trending papers / daily papers / paper of the day: ls hf://papers/trending, ls hf://papers/daily/latest
- search models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, or docs: search hf://models QUERY
- read a known file: cat hf://models/OWNER/NAME/README.md

Other advertised Hub tools can search or inspect a known repo id. Use hf_whoami for the current Hugging Face account.

hf:// URIs can be converted to browser URLs by replacing hf://buckets/OWNER/NAME/PATH with https://huggingface.co/buckets/OWNER/NAME/resolve/PATH; for models, datasets, and spaces, use https://huggingface.co[/datasets|/spaces]/OWNER/NAME/resolve/main/PATH. URL-encode each path segment.

arXiv paper ids (for example 2502.16161) are often used as references between datasets, models, and papers. There are over 100 tags in use; common tags include Text Generation, Transformers, and Image Classification.
Hugging Face tools are being used by authenticated user 'LBJLincoln26'

## Supabase
Here are guidelines for using Supabase tools effectively:

- Before making schema changes, use `list_tables` to understand the existing structure
- When debugging issues, start with `get_logs` and `get_advisors` before making changes
- Use `get_project_url` and `get_publishable_api_key` when helping users configure client-side integrations

If you have access to a local development environment with a filesystem and shell:
- Install the Supabase agent skill for critical development and security guidance: `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/ai-skills.md)
- Use the Supabase CLI (`supabase`) for local development workflows such as starting a local stack, managing migrations, and running edge functions locally (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development.md)
- Prefer local development and testing before applying changes to a remote project

If you are running in a web-only or remote environment without filesystem or shell access:
- Rely on the MCP tools directly for all Supabase interactions
- Use `apply_migration` carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

## Firecrawl
Firecrawl provides web, developer, and research search. Use firecrawl_search to find relevant results across the web and specialized indexes. For a programming question, firecrawl_developer_search searches indexed repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and curated documentation sites and returns the matched passages, and skills: "only" narrows it to agent-skill files; firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"] reaches the same index beside ordinary web results, returning the hits in the web group rather than as passages and offering no skills filter. For a biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature question, the firecrawl_research_* tools search the paper index, while categories: ["research"] on firecrawl_search filters ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites. Use the firecrawl_research_* tools to search academic and research literature, expand from anchor papers via the citation graph, and read full-text passages from a specific paper. All tools are read-only and return ranked results.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

87	
88	/** One registration plus the layer name every read reports for it. */
89	interface StoredComponent {
90	  readonly descriptor: ComponentDescriptor
91	  readonly layer: ComponentLayer
92	}
93	
94	/** Copy a descriptor so callers never share the registry's stored arrays. */
95	function detach(descriptor: ComponentDescriptor): ComponentDescriptor {
96	  return {
97	    ...descriptor,
98	    ...descriptor.members === undefined ? {} : { members: [...descriptor.members] },
99	  }
100	}
101	
102	/** Detach one stored registration into the view a caller reads. */
103	function viewOf(stored: StoredComponent): ComponentView {
104	  return { ...detach(stored.descriptor), layer: stored.layer }
105	}
106	
107	/**
108	 * One scope's component registrations. The context-global layer reports
109	 * `global` and every scoped overlay reports `agent`: a deeper chain still
110	 * reads as `agent`, because a subagent records its own composition.
111	 */
112	class ComponentScopeLayer implements ScopeLayer {
113	  readonly components: NamedEntries<StoredComponent>
114	  /** Layer name reported for every registration filed here. */
115	  readonly name: ComponentLayer
116	
117	  constructor(scope: ScopeKey | undefined) {
118	    this.name = scope === undefined ? 'global' : 'agent'
119	    this.components = new NamedEntries(id => new ComponentError(
120	      scope === undefined
121	        ? `component "${id}" is already registered`
122	        : `component "${id}" is already registered in this scope`,
123	      'COMPONENT_DUPLICATE_ID',
124	    ))
125	  }
126	
127	  /** Whether this aggregate layer holds no registration. */
128	  isEmpty(): boolean {
129	    return this.components.isEmpty()
130	  }
131	}
132	
133	/** Component registry (`ctx.components`): the composition-time inventory mirrored from live seams. */
134	export class ComponentRegistry extends Service {
135	  private readonly layers = new ScopedLayers<ComponentScopeLayer>(
136	    scope => new ComponentScopeLayer(scope),
137	    // No change notification: nothing follows registry edges, and a consumer
138	    // that needs the current inventory reads it. The event belongs with its
139	    // first subscriber.
140	    () => {},
141	  )
142	
143	  constructor(ctx: Context) {
144	    super(ctx, 'components')
145	  }
146	
147	  /**
148	   * Register one component into the calling context's layer: an unscoped
149	   * context (a host row or repository plugin) registers globally, while a
150	   * scoped context (an agent preset's standing mount) registers for that
151	   * scope alone. Registrations are effects: the producer keeps the returned
152	   * disposer under its own fiber so disposal removes the component.
153	   * @param descriptor - complete component description, including the digest its producer computed.
154	   * @returns the exact disposer that removes this registration and no later one under the same id.
155	   * @throws {@link ComponentError} when the id is already registered in the same layer.
156	   */
157	  register(descriptor: ComponentDescriptor): () => void {
158	    const stored = detach(descriptor)
159	    return this.layers.effect(
160	      this.ctx,
161	      layer => layer.components.insert(stored.id, { descriptor: stored, layer: layer.name }),
162	      { label: 'components.register()' },
163	    )
164	  }
165	
166	  /**
167	   * Read one component as a scope sees it.
168	   * @param id - component identity.
169	   * @param options - read options; `scope` selects the viewing agent's layers.
170	   * @returns a detached view carrying its winning layer, or `undefined` when the id is absent.
171	   */
172	  get(id: ComponentIdType, options: ComponentViewOptions = {}): ComponentView | undefined {
173	    const stored = this.view(options.scope).get(id)
174	    return stored === undefined ? undefined : viewOf(stored)
175	  }
176	
177	  /**
178	   * List components as a scope sees them, in registration order with the
179	   * global layer first.
180	   * @param options - read options; `scope` selects the viewing agent's layers and `kind` filters by kind.
181	   * @returns detached views carrying their winning layer.
182	   */
183	  list(options: ComponentListOptions = {}): ComponentView[] {
184	    const kind = options.kind
185	    return [...this.view(options.scope).values()]
186	      .filter(stored => kind === undefined || stored.descriptor.kind === kind)
187	      .map(viewOf)
188	  }
189	
190	  /**
191	   * Effective registrations for one viewing scope: the global layer followed
192	   * by the scope chain farthest ancestor first, so the nearest layer's entry
193	   * wins a duplicate id.
194	   */
195	  private view(scope: ScopeKey | undefined): Map<string, StoredComponent> {
196	    return this.layers.merge(scope, layer => layer.components)
197	  }
198	}
199	
200	export default ComponentRegistry

# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` with no compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
```
