  util/        zero-dependency utilities

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and safe residue from deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns this signal
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When required `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; do not merge before checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, and real-API e2e for provider behavior.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or for an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

## Editing these instructions

`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when the required content genuinely needs more space.

## Vendoring policy

`vendor/` packages are pinned source copies (manifest with upstream SHAs in [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)). Update via the sync procedure there; re-apply or retire the logged local modifications; rerun `pnpm run test && pnpm run build`.

- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

## Editing these instructions

`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when the required content genuinely needs more space.

## Vendoring policy

`vendor/` packages are pinned source copies (manifest with upstream SHAs in [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)). Update via the sync procedure there; re-apply or retire the logged local modifications; rerun `pnpm run test && pnpm run build`.

</system-reminder>

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

1	/**
2	 * Mirrors subagent providers into the component registry as `agent-provider`
3	 * components, following the subagent seam's own provider events.
4	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents
5	 */
6	
7	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
8	import { ComponentId, componentDigest } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
9	import type {
10	  ComponentDescriptor,
11	  ComponentDigest,
12	  ComponentId as ComponentIdType,
13	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types'
14	// Type-only: resolves ctx.subagents and the subagent lifecycle events.
15	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
16	
17	export const name = 'components-subagents'
18	export const inject = ['components', 'subagents']
19	
20	/** Kind-specific detail of an `agent-provider` component. */
21	export interface AgentProviderComponentDetail {
22	  /** Provider name as registered with `ctx.subagents`. */
23	  readonly provider: string
24	}
25	
26	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types' {
27	  interface ComponentKindMap {
28	    /**
29	     * One subagent provider registered with `ctx.subagents`. The callable
30	     * route is the `subagent` tool instance configured for the provider; the
31	     * subagent seam does not expose that binding, so the component carries
32	     * no `invoke` pointer.
33	     */
34	    'agent-provider': AgentProviderComponentDetail
35	  }
36	}
37	
38	const OWNER = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents'
39	
40	/**
41	 * Component id of one subagent provider.
42	 * @param provider - provider name as registered with `ctx.subagents`.
43	 * @returns the stable id `agent-provider:<provider>`.
44	 */
45	export function agentProviderComponentId(provider: string): ComponentIdType {
46	  return ComponentId(`agent-provider:${provider}`)
47	}
48	
49	/**
50	 * Content address of one `agent-provider` component. The canonical value is
51	 * `[provider]`, so the digest addresses the registration and not the agent
52	 * the provider starts: the subagent seam exposes a provider name and its
53	 * lifecycle edges, never the composition behind them, which is why this kind's
54	 * `digestBasis` is `registration`.
55	 * @param provider - provider name as registered with `ctx.subagents`.
56	 * @returns the digest over this kind and that canonical value.
57	 */
58	export function agentProviderDigest(provider: string): ComponentDigest {
59	  return componentDigest('agent-provider', [provider])
60	}
61	
62	/** Describe one provider as a component. */
63	function describeProvider(provider: string): ComponentDescriptor {
64	  return {
65	    id: agentProviderComponentId(provider),
66	    kind: 'agent-provider',
67	    digest: agentProviderDigest(provider),
68	    digestBasis: 'registration',
69	    name: provider,
70	    description: `Subagent provider "${provider}", reached through the subagent tool instance configured for it.`,
71	    owner: OWNER,
72	    provenance: 'curated',
73	    detail: { provider },
74	  }
75	}
76	
77	/**
78	 * Register every current provider and follow later additions and removals.
79	 * @param ctx - Cordis context carrying the component registry and the subagent seam.
80	 */
81	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
82	  const disposers = new Map<string, () => void>()
83	  const add = (provider: string): void => {
84	    if (disposers.has(provider)) return
85	    disposers.set(provider, ctx.components.register(describeProvider(provider)))
86	  }
87	  const remove = (provider: string): void => {
88	    const dispose = disposers.get(provider)
89	    if (dispose === undefined) return
90	    disposers.delete(provider)
91	    dispose()
92	  }
93	  for (const provider of ctx.subagents.list()) add(provider)
94	  ctx.on('subagent/provider-added', (provider) => { add(provider.name) })
95	  ctx.on('subagent/provider-removed', (provider) => { remove(provider) })
96	  ctx.effect(() => () => {
97	    for (const dispose of disposers.values()) dispose()
98	    disposers.clear()
99	  }, 'components-subagents teardown')
100	}
101

1	/**
2	 * Mirrors the tools one scope sees into the component registry as `tool`
3	 * components, following the tool registry's own `tools/change` notification.
4	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-components-tools
5	 */
6	
7	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
8	import { ComponentId, componentDigest } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
9	import type {
10	  ComponentCanonical,
11	  ComponentDescriptor,
12	  ComponentDigest,
13	  ComponentId as ComponentIdType,
14	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types'
15	import type { ToolSchema } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
16	import { scopeOf } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope'
17	// Type-only: resolves ctx.tools and the registry's `tools/change` notification.
18	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'
19	
20	export const name = 'components-tools'
21	export const inject = ['components', 'tools']
22	
23	/** Kind-specific detail of a `tool` component. */
24	export interface ToolComponentDetail {
25	  /** Model-facing tool name as `ctx.tools.schemas()` projects it. */
26	  readonly toolName: string
27	}
28	
29	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types' {
30	  interface ComponentKindMap {
31	    /**
32	     * One tool the adapter's own scope sees, as the model sees it. A tool
33	     * removed from that scope — unregistered, restricted away, or collapsed by
34	     * a presentation mode — leaves the inventory with it.
35	     */
36	    'tool': ToolComponentDetail
37	  }
38	}
39	
40	const OWNER = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-tools'
41	
42	/**
43	 * Component id of one tool.
44	 * @param toolName - the model-facing tool name.
45	 * @returns the stable id `tool:<name>`.
46	 */
47	export function toolComponentId(toolName: string): ComponentIdType {
48	  return ComponentId(`tool:${toolName}`)
49	}
50	
51	/**
52	 * Content address of one `tool` component. The canonical value is the
53	 * model-facing schema exactly as `ctx.tools.schemas(scope)` projects it — name,
54	 * description, and parameter schema, in the registry's own field order — so one
55	 * byte changed in a parameter description moves the digest and nothing the
56	 * registry computes per assembly enters it.
57	 * @param schema - one projected schema from `ctx.tools.schemas(scope)`.
58	 * @returns the digest over this kind and that canonical value.
59	 */
60	export function toolDigest(schema: ToolSchema): ComponentDigest {
61	  // `schemas()` materializes each projection as lossless JSON, so the cast
62	  // records what the projection already is rather than re-encoding it.
63	  return componentDigest('tool', schema as unknown as ComponentCanonical)
64	}
65	
66	/** Describe one projected schema as a component. */
67	function describeTool(schema: ToolSchema, digest: ComponentDigest): ComponentDescriptor {
68	  return {
69	    id: toolComponentId(schema.name),
70	    kind: 'tool',
71	    digest,
72	    digestBasis: 'content',
73	    name: schema.name,
74	    description: schema.description,
75	    owner: OWNER,
76	    provenance: 'curated',
77	    invoke: { tool: schema.name },
78	    detail: { toolName: schema.name },
79	  }
80	}
81	
82	/** One mirrored tool: the digest that produced it and the disposer that removes it. */
83	interface MirroredTool {
84	  readonly digest: ComponentDigest
85	  readonly dispose: () => void
86	}
87	
88	/**
89	 * Mirror the visible tools of `ctx`'s own scope and follow every later change.
90	 *
91	 * The registry publishes one unfiltered `tools/change` for a registration, a
92	 * disposal, and a scoped restriction alike, and reports no diff with it, so the
93	 * adapter recomputes the visible set and reconciles: a tool whose schema is
94	 * unchanged keeps its registration, a changed one is replaced under the same id,
95	 * and one that left the scope is disposed.
96	 * @param ctx - Cordis context carrying the component registry and the tool registry.
97	 */
98	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
99	  const mirrored = new Map<string, MirroredTool>()
100	  const scope = scopeOf(ctx)
101	  const sync = (): void => {
102	    const present = new Set<string>()
103	    for (const schema of ctx.tools.schemas(scope)) {
104	      present.add(schema.name)
105	      const digest = toolDigest(schema)
106	      const current = mirrored.get(schema.name)
107	      if (current?.digest === digest) continue
108	      current?.dispose()
109	      mirrored.set(schema.name, { digest, dispose: ctx.components.register(describeTool(schema, digest)) })
110	    }
111	    for (const [toolName, entry] of [...mirrored]) {
112	      if (present.has(toolName)) continue
113	      mirrored.delete(toolName)
114	      entry.dispose()
115	    }
116	  }
117	  sync()
118	  ctx.on('tools/change', sync)
119	  ctx.effect(() => () => {
120	    for (const entry of mirrored.values()) entry.dispose()
121	    mirrored.clear()
122	  }, 'components-tools teardown')
123	}
124

1	/**
2	 * Composition manifest writer. Before every proposed step it recomputes the
3	 * components the calling agent has in play, addresses the whole set with one
4	 * `compositionSha256`, and appends a `composition/manifest` event only when
5	 * that hash differs from the last one the session log recorded.
6	 *
7	 * Recomputing rather than tracking incrementally is what keeps the record
8	 * correct across a producer's HMR disposal, a preset mounted after creation,
9	 * and scope shadowing: the writer holds no subscription state any of those
10	 * orderings could invalidate.
11	 *
12	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-components-manifest
13	 */
14	
15	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
16	import type { PreStepDecision } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
17	// Type-only: resolves ctx.components and the registry's read options.
18	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
19	import { buildCompositionManifest, lastCompositionManifest } from './fold.ts'
20	
21	// The pure payload outlet (./types.ts, the ONE home of the
22	// `composition/manifest` declaration) re-exported onto the package root keeps
23	// the module edge in the emitted index.d.ts, so aggregate programs consuming
24	// the declaration still receive the SessionEventMap merge.
25	export type * from './types.ts'
26	export { COMPOSITION_MANIFEST_VERSION } from './types.ts'
27	export {
28	  buildCompositionManifest, compositionSha256, isComponentAddress, lastCompositionManifest, manifestEntries,
29	} from './fold.ts'
30	
31	/** Cordis plugin name used by loader diagnostics. */
32	export const name = 'components-manifest'
33	
34	/** The agent registry that owns pre-step processing, and the inventory the manifest records. */
35	export const inject = ['agents', 'components']
36	
37	/**
38	 * Record the composition before every proposed step.
39	 *
40	 * `next()` runs first so the reading covers what the whole pre-step chain
41	 * settled on, and the manifest is written for the step that was proposed even
42	 * when a later policy rejected it: the composition was in play either way, and
43	 * the deduplication key keeps a stable one to exactly one event.
44	 * @param ctx - plugin context; the listener is disposed with it.
45	 */
46	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
47	  ctx.on('agent/pre-step', async ({ agent }, next): Promise<PreStepDecision> => {
48	    const decision = await next()
49	    const manifest = buildCompositionManifest(ctx.components.list({ scope: agent }))
50	    if (lastCompositionManifest(agent.session.events)?.compositionSha256 !== manifest.compositionSha256) {
51	      agent.session.append('composition/manifest', manifest)
52	    }
53	    return decision
54	  })

5	 * service imports so the writer, the fold, and the invariant companion share
6	 * one home.
7	 *
8	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-components-manifest/types
9	 */
10	
11	import type {
12	  ComponentDigest,
13	  ComponentDigestBasis,
14	  ComponentId,
15	  ComponentKind,
16	  ComponentLayer,
17	  ComponentProvenance,
18	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types'

21	export const COMPOSITION_MANIFEST_VERSION = 1
22	
23	/** One component in play, as the manifest records it. */
24	export interface CompositionManifestEntry {
25	  /** Stable component identity; with {@link digest} it forms the `id@digest` address. */
26	  readonly id: ComponentId
27	  /** Content address of the generation in play. */
28	  readonly digest: ComponentDigest
29	  /** The component's declared kind. */
30	  readonly kind: ComponentKind
31	  /** Whether the digest covers the component's own bytes or only its registration. */
32	  readonly digestBasis: ComponentDigestBasis
33	  /** Whether people curated the component or an agent synthesized it. */
34	  readonly provenance: ComponentProvenance
35	  /** Component this generation derived from, absent for roots. */
36	  readonly lineage?: ComponentId
37	  /** Registry layer the winning registration sat in for the recording agent. */
38	  readonly layer: ComponentLayer

42	export interface CompositionManifest {
43	  /** Payload version, so a later field addition is readable against a stated shape. */
44	  readonly version: typeof COMPOSITION_MANIFEST_VERSION
45	  /** Every component in play, ordered by `id@digest` address. */
46	  readonly components: readonly CompositionManifestEntry[]
47	  /** Lowercase SHA-256 hex over the ordered addresses joined by newlines. */
48	  readonly compositionSha256: string
49	}

52	  interface SessionEventMap {
53	    /**
54	     * Every component one agent had in play when a step was proposed: its
55	     * `id@digest` address, kind, digest basis, provenance, lineage, and the
56	     * registry layer the winning registration sat in, ordered by address, with
57	     * `compositionSha256` hashing that ordered address list. Log-only, and
58	     * written only when the hash differs from the last manifest in the same
59	     * log, so a stable composition records exactly one event and a resumed
60	     * session re-emits nothing. Required on read: a build that cannot

1	/**
2	 * Pure derivations over the composition manifest: the address list one registry
3	 * reading produces, the hash that addresses the whole set, and the last
4	 * manifest a durable log recorded.
5	 *
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-components-manifest/fold
7	 */
8	
9	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
10	import { componentAddress } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
11	import type { ComponentView } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types'
12	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
13	import { COMPOSITION_MANIFEST_VERSION } from './types.ts'
14	import type { CompositionManifest, CompositionManifestEntry } from './types.ts'
15	
16	/** An `id@digest` address whose digest is a full lowercase SHA-256 hex. */
17	const ADDRESS = /^[^\n@]+@[0-9a-f]{64}$/
18	
19	/**
20	 * Whether one `id@digest` address is well-formed: a non-empty id carrying no
21	 * separator and no newline, then the full 64-character lowercase digest a
22	 * comparison keys on.
23	 * @param address - the candidate address.
24	 * @returns whether the address can be compared against another generation's.
25	 */
26	export function isComponentAddress(address: string): boolean {
27	  return ADDRESS.test(address)
28	}
29	
30	/**
31	 * Hash one ordered address list.
32	 * @param addresses - the `id@digest` addresses in manifest order.
33	 * @returns the lowercase SHA-256 hex over the addresses joined by newlines.
34	 */
35	export function compositionSha256(addresses: readonly string[]): string {
36	  return createHash('sha256').update(addresses.join('\n')).digest('hex')
37	}
38	
39	/**
40	 * Project one registry reading onto the manifest entries, ordered by address so
41	 * two hosts that composed the same set hash it identically.
42	 * @param views - the components one agent sees, as `ctx.components.list()` returns them.
43	 * @returns one entry per component, ascending by `id@digest`.
44	 */
45	export function manifestEntries(views: readonly ComponentView[]): CompositionManifestEntry[] {
46	  return views
47	    .map((view): CompositionManifestEntry => ({
48	      id: view.id,
49	      digest: view.digest,
50	      kind: view.kind,
51	      digestBasis: view.digestBasis,
52	      provenance: view.provenance,
53	      ...view.lineage === undefined ? {} : { lineage: view.lineage },
54	      layer: view.layer,
55	    }))
56	    // Code-unit comparison, so the order is identical on every machine.
57	    .sort((left, right) => {
58	      const a = componentAddress(left.id, left.digest)
59	      const b = componentAddress(right.id, right.digest)
60	      return a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0
61	    })
62	}
63	
64	/**
65	 * Build the durable manifest of one registry reading.
66	 * @param views - the components one agent sees, as `ctx.components.list()` returns them.
67	 * @returns the payload to append, hashed over its own ordered addresses.
68	 */
69	export function buildCompositionManifest(views: readonly ComponentView[]): CompositionManifest {
70	  const components = manifestEntries(views)
71	  return {
72	    version: COMPOSITION_MANIFEST_VERSION,
73	    components,
74	    compositionSha256: compositionSha256(components.map(entry => componentAddress(entry.id, entry.digest))),
75	  }
76	}
77	
78	/**
79	 * The newest manifest a durable log recorded.
80	 * @param events - the session's event log, oldest first.
81	 * @returns the last recorded manifest, or `undefined` when the log holds none.
82	 */
83	export function lastCompositionManifest(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): CompositionManifest | undefined {
84	  for (let index = events.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
85	    const event = events[index]
86	    if (event?.type === 'composition/manifest') return event.data
87	  }
88	  return undefined
89	}

1	/**
2	 * Package-owned invariant over the durable record this package writes.
3	 *
4	 * Two manifests in a row that state the same `compositionSha256` would mean the
5	 * writer appended a record no composition change produced, which is exactly the
6	 * deduplication a consumer folding the log relies on. Every entry must also
7	 * carry a comparable address: an id with no separator and no newline, and the
8	 * full 64-character lowercase digest, because a truncated or malformed one
9	 * silently fails every generation comparison keyed on it.
10	 *
11	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-components-manifest/invariant
12	 */
13	
14	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
15	import { componentAddress } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
16	import type { InvariantFailure, InvariantInstaller } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants'
17	import type { Session, SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
18	import { isComponentAddress, lastCompositionManifest } from './fold.ts'
19	import type { CompositionManifest } from './types.ts'
20	
21	const PACKAGE_NAME = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-manifest'
22	
23	/** Cordis companion plugin name. */
24	export const name = 'components-manifest-invariant'
25	/** Service required before the companion can reserve package ownership. */
26	export const inject = ['invariants']
27	
28	/** Validate one recorded manifest against the durable prefix that precedes it. */
29	function validateManifest(
30	  prior: readonly SessionEvent[],
31	  manifest: CompositionManifest,
32	  fail: InvariantFailure,
33	): void {
34	  const previous = lastCompositionManifest(prior)
35	  if (previous?.compositionSha256 === manifest.compositionSha256) {
36	    fail(`composition/manifest repeats compositionSha256 ${manifest.compositionSha256}, which the preceding manifest already recorded`)
37	  }
38	  for (const entry of manifest.components) {
39	    const address = componentAddress(entry.id, entry.digest)
40	    if (isComponentAddress(address)) continue
41	    fail(`composition/manifest lists component address ${JSON.stringify(address)}, which no generation comparison can key on`)
42	  }
43	}
44	
45	/** Validate one candidate event against the durable prefix that precedes it. */
46	function validateEvent(
47	  prior: readonly SessionEvent[],
48	  event: SessionEvent,
49	  fail: InvariantFailure,
50	): void {
51	  if (event.type === 'composition/manifest') validateManifest(prior, event.data, fail)
52	}
53	
54	/** Check existing sessions and every candidate event before Session publishes it. */
55	const install: InvariantInstaller = Object.assign((ctx: Context, fail: InvariantFailure) => {
56	  for (const session of ctx.sessions.list()) {
57	    const prior: SessionEvent[] = []
58	    for (const event of session.events) {
59	      validateEvent(prior, event, fail)
60	      prior.push(event)
61	    }
62	  }
63	  /* jscpd:ignore-start -- package companions share dispatch and registration plumbing */
64	  ctx.on('internal/dispatch', (_mode, eventName, args) => {
65	    if (eventName !== 'session/event') return
66	    const [session, event] = args as [Session, SessionEvent]
67	    validateEvent(session.events, event, fail)
68	  }, { global: true })
69	}, { inject: ['sessions'] })
70	
71	/**
72	 * Register the composition-manifest invariant companion.
73	 * @param ctx - Cordis context carrying the invariant service.
74	 * @returns the installed registration's disposer after setup succeeds.
75	 */
76	export const apply = (ctx: Context): Promise<() => void> =>
77	  Promise.resolve(ctx.invariants.register(PACKAGE_NAME, install))
78	/* jscpd:ignore-end */

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Test driver: boot the composition-manifest composition, compose one session
 * from the `manifest` preset, and run three turns — two over an unchanged
 * composition and one after registering a tool into the global layer — so the
 * persisted log states exactly one manifest per composition change.
 */

import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
import { runFixtureTurn } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke'
import { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'

const configPath = process.argv[2]
if (configPath === undefined) throw new Error('composition-manifest driver requires a config path')

const ctx = await boot('composition-manifest-e2e', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
try {
  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the driver creates the agent only over the settled application.
  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
  const created = await ctx.agents.create({
    sessionId: SessionId('composition-manifest'),
    meta: { cwd: process.cwd() },
    agentOptions: { provider: 'manifest-mock', model: 'manifest-mock' },
    setup: async (agentCtx: Context) => void await ctx.agentPresets.mount(agentCtx, 'manifest'),
  })
  try {
    await runFixtureTurn(ctx, { task: 'first turn' })
    await runFixtureTurn(ctx, { task: 'second turn over the same composition' })

    // A tool registered into the global layer after two turns: the tools
    // adapter follows `tools/change`, so the next step records a new manifest.
    ctx.tools.register({
      name: 'late_note',
      description: 'Record one note, registered after the session started.',
      parameters: { type: 'object', properties: {} },
      output: {
        schema: { type: 'string' },
        render: (_args: unknown, value: unknown) => [{ type: 'text' as const, text: String(value) }],
      },
      execute: () => Promise.resolve('noted'),
    })
    await runFixtureTurn(ctx, { task: 'third turn after the tool was added' })

    process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({ type: 'result', sessionId: created.agent.session.id })}\n`)
  } finally {
    await created.dispose()
  }
} finally {
  await ctx.fiber.dispose()
}

import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
import {
  LlmAdapter,
  type GenerateOptions,
  type LlmResolvedModelInfo,
  type StreamChunk,
} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'

/**
 * Keyless adapter that answers every request with one text block and calls no
 * tool, so each turn is exactly one step and the manifest events a session
 * records are decided by composition changes alone.
 */
class ManifestMockAdapter extends LlmAdapter {
  override resolveModel(provider: string, model: string): Promise<LlmResolvedModelInfo> {
    return Promise.resolve({ provider, id: model, name: model })
  }

  async * stream(options: GenerateOptions): AsyncIterable<StreamChunk> {
    const last = options.messages.at(-1)?.content.find(block => block.type === 'text')
    const reply = `recorded: ${last?.type === 'text' ? last.text : 'nothing'}`
    yield { type: 'block-start', index: 0, blockType: 'text' }
    yield { type: 'text-delta', index: 0, text: reply }
    yield { type: 'block-end', index: 0, block: { type: 'text', text: reply } }
    yield { type: 'usage', usage: { inputTokens: 5, outputTokens: 3 } }
    yield { type: 'finish', reason: { kind: 'stop' } }
  }
}

export const name = 'manifest-mock-llm'
export const inject = ['llm']

/**
 * Register the keyless `manifest-mock` adapter.
 * @param ctx - plugin context carrying the LLM runtime.
 */
export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
  ctx.llm.registerAdapter(['manifest-mock'], new ManifestMockAdapter())
}

402	/**

404	 * in the text — the same word-boundary shape the transcript chip decoration
405	 * uses, so a gesture reads as one wherever it sits in the sentence. A second

413	 * first-seen order. Every text block of direct user input is scanned; no
414	 * other source can forge a gesture.

408	   * @param requestId - Request identity to settle once.
409	   * @param resolution - Browser refusal or exact Client activation result.
410	   * @returns Whether the still-pending request accepted this resolution.
411	   */
412	  @Remote('resolveRequestRun')
413	  async resolveRequestRun(
414	    requestId: ApprovalRequestId,
415	    resolution: DynamicCordisRunResolution,
416	  ): Promise<DynamicCordisResolveAck> {
417	    const pending = this.registry.peekRequest(requestId)
418	    if (pending === undefined) return { accepted: false }
419	    const plugin = this.registry.get(pending.pluginId)
420	    if (resolution.ok && plugin?.run?.pluginRunId !== resolution.pluginRunId) return { accepted: false }
421	    if (!resolution.ok && resolution.pluginRunId !== undefined
422	      && plugin?.run?.pluginRunId !== resolution.pluginRunId) return { accepted: false }
423	    this.registry.claimRequest(requestId)
424	    const settled = await this.settleActivation(plugin, resolution, requestId)
425	    this.announceResolved(requestId, resolution, pending.requiresApproval ? undefined : 'completed')
426	    this.steerRunOutcome(pending, settled)
427	    return { accepted: true }
428	  }

768	  private resolvePlan(
769	    agent: Agent,
770	    pluginId: CordisDynamicPluginId,
771	    packageId: CordisDynamicPackageId,
772	    mode: CordisDynamicRunMode,
773	    allowActiveAttach = false,
774	  ): { ok: true } & ActivationPlan | { ok: false; response: Extract<DynamicCordisRunResponse, { ok: false }> } {
775	    const plugin = this.owned(agent, pluginId)
776	    if (plugin === undefined) return { ok: false, response: { ok: false, reason: 'plugin-missing', message: missingPluginMessage(pluginId) } }
777	    const definition = plugin.packages.get(packageId)
778	    if (definition === undefined) {
779	      return { ok: false, response: { ok: false, reason: 'package-missing', message: `plugin "${pluginId}" has no package "${packageId}"` } }
780	    }
781	    const current = plugin.currentPackageId
782	    if (mode === 'update' && (current === undefined || current === packageId)) {
783	      return {
784	        ok: false,
785	        response: {
786	          ok: false,
787	          reason: 'invalid-mode',
788	          message: current === undefined
789	            ? `plugin "${pluginId}" has no successful version yet; start "${packageId}" with mode "run"`
790	            : `package "${packageId}" is already current; use mode "run"`,
791	        },
792	      }
793	    }
794	    if (mode === 'run' && current !== undefined && current !== packageId) {
795	      return {
796	        ok: false,
797	        response: {
798	          ok: false,
799	          reason: 'invalid-mode',
800	          message: `package "${packageId}" differs from current "${current}"; use mode "update"`,
801	        },
802	      }
803	    }
804	    if (!allowActiveAttach && this.starting.has(pluginId)) {
805	      return { ok: false, response: { ok: false, reason: 'transition-in-flight', message: `plugin "${pluginId}" is already starting` } }
806	    }
807	    return { ok: true, plugin, definition, mode }
808	  }

810	  private activate(
811	    plan: ActivationPlan,
812	    requestId: ApprovalRequestId | undefined,
813	    allowActiveAttach: boolean,
814	    attempt: DynamicCordisRunAttempt,
815	  ): Promise<DynamicCordisHostHalfResult> {
816	    const inFlight = this.starting.get(plan.plugin.pluginId)
817	    if (inFlight !== undefined) return inFlight
818	    const starting = this.startFresh(plan, requestId, allowActiveAttach, attempt)
819	    this.starting.set(plan.plugin.pluginId, starting)
820	    return starting.finally(() => { this.starting.delete(plan.plugin.pluginId) })

823	  private async startFresh(
824	    plan: ActivationPlan,
825	    requestId: ApprovalRequestId | undefined,
826	    allowActiveAttach: boolean,
827	    attempt: DynamicCordisRunAttempt,
828	  ): Promise<DynamicCordisHostHalfResult> {
829	    const { plugin, definition, mode } = plan
830	    if (allowActiveAttach
831	      && plugin.run?.packageId === definition.packageId
832	      && plugin.run.pluginRunId === attempt.pluginRunId) {
833	      return {
834	        ok: true,
835	        pluginId: plugin.pluginId,
836	        packageId: definition.packageId,
837	        pluginRunId: plugin.run.pluginRunId,
838	        waitingFor: missingFor(this.ctx, plugin.run),
839	        startedHere: false,
840	      }
841	    }
842	    if (plugin.run !== undefined) await this.retract(plugin)
843	    if (mode === 'update' || plugin.currentPackageId === undefined) plugin.nextPackageId = definition.packageId
844	    const run: DynamicCordisRun = {
845	      pluginRunId: attempt.pluginRunId,
846	      packageId: definition.packageId,
847	      handlers: new Map(),
848	      handlerDisposers: [],
849	      reportedRuntimeErrors: new Set(),
850	      ...requestId === undefined ? {} : { startedForRequest: requestId },
851	    }
852	    if (definition.hostCode !== undefined) {
853	      const failure = await this.startHost(plugin, definition.hostCode, run)
854	      if (failure !== undefined) return { ok: false, ...failure }
855	    }
856	    plugin.run = run
857	    this.ctx.emit('cordis/dynamic-package', {
858	      pluginId: plugin.pluginId,
859	      packageId: definition.packageId,
860	      pluginRunId: run.pluginRunId,
861	      name: definition.name,
862	    })
863	    attempt.host = {
864	      status: run.fiber === undefined ? 'absent' : missingFor(this.ctx, run).length === 0 ? 'running' : 'waiting',
865	      waitingFor: missingFor(this.ctx, run),
866	    }
867	    if (definition.clientCode === undefined) {
868	      this.commitActivation(plugin, run)
869	    } else {
870	      attempt.status = 'client-pending'
871	      attempt.client = { status: 'pending', waitingFor: [] }
872	    }
873	    return {
874	      ok: true,
875	      pluginId: plugin.pluginId,
876	      packageId: definition.packageId,
877	      pluginRunId: run.pluginRunId,
878	      waitingFor: missingFor(this.ctx, run),
879	      startedHere: true,
880	    }
881	  }

883	  private async startHost(
884	    plugin: DynamicCordisPlugin,
885	    hostCode: string,
886	    run: DynamicCordisRun,
887	  ): Promise<CordisErrorDetails | undefined> {
888	    const handle = (method: unknown, fn: unknown): (() => void) => {
889	      const normalized = normalizeHandler(method, fn)
890	      run.handlers.set(normalized.method, normalized.handler)
891	      const dispose = (): void => {
892	        if (run.handlers.get(normalized.method) === normalized.handler) run.handlers.delete(normalized.method)
893	      }
894	      run.handlerDisposers.push(dispose)
895	      return dispose
896	    }
897	    try {
898	      const sandbox = createSandbox(plugin.pluginId, { handle })
899	      const evaluated = await evaluateHostCode(sandbox, hostCode, plugin.pluginId, this.resolved.vmTimeoutMs)
900	      if (!isPlugin(evaluated)) {
901	        throw new Error(evaluated === undefined
902	          ? 'the Host half returned `undefined` — did you forget `return`?'
903	          : 'the Host half must return a Plugin function or an object with apply(ctx)')
904	      }
905	      run.fiber = await startHostHalf(
906	        this.requireGroup(),
907	        evaluated,
908	        (error) => { this.steerGuardFailure(plugin, run, 'Host', errorDetails(error)) },
909	      )
910	      return undefined
911	    } catch (error) {
912	      for (const dispose of run.handlerDisposers.splice(0)) dispose()
913	      return errorDetails(error)
914	    }
915	  }

917	  private async settleActivation(
918	    plugin: DynamicCordisPlugin | undefined,
919	    resolution: DynamicCordisRunResolution,
920	    requestId?: ApprovalRequestId,
921	  ): Promise<DynamicCordisRunResponse> {
922	    if (plugin === undefined) return { ok: false, reason: 'plugin-missing', message: 'the dynamic plugin was removed during activation' }
923	    const attempt = plugin.latestRun
924	    if (!resolution.ok) {
925	      if (resolution.reason === 'rejected') {
926	        if (attempt !== undefined) {
927	          attempt.status = 'rejected'
928	          attempt.error = this.diagnostic(plugin, attempt, 'approval', resolution.message ?? 'the run request was declined')
929	          attempt.client = { status: 'stopped', waitingFor: [] }
930	        }
931	        return { ok: false, reason: 'rejected', message: resolution.message ?? 'the run request was declined' }
932	      }
933	      const run = plugin.run
934	      const ownsRun = run !== undefined
935	        && resolution.pluginRunId === run.pluginRunId
936	        && (requestId === undefined || run.startedForRequest === requestId)
937	        && resolution.startedHere !== false
938	      if (ownsRun) await this.retract(plugin)
939	      if (attempt !== undefined && (resolution.pluginRunId === undefined || attempt.pluginRunId === resolution.pluginRunId)) {
940	        this.failAttempt(
941	          plugin,
942	          attempt,
943	          resolution.reason === 'host-half-failed' ? 'host-apply' : 'client-apply',

1	/**
2	 * Mirrors every standing agent-preset mount into the component registry as
3	 * `preset` components, reconciled against the roster's own live-mount reading
4	 * whenever an agent joins a composition or a session commits a different one.
5	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-components-presets
6	 */
7	
8	import { dirname, isAbsolute, relative, sep } from 'node:path'
9	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
10	// Type-only: resolves the `agent/created` lifecycle notification.
11	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
12	import { livePresetMounts } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets'
13	import type { PresetMount, PresetTrust } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets'
14	// Type-only: resolves the roster's `agent-preset/selected` notification.
15	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets/types'
16	import { ComponentId, componentDigest } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
17	import type {
18	  ComponentCanonical,
19	  ComponentDescriptor,
20	  ComponentDigest,
21	  ComponentId as ComponentIdType,
22	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types'
23	import { snapshotJsonValue } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
24	
25	export const name = 'components-presets'
26	// `agentPresets` is the seam this adapter mirrors even though the mount reading
27	// is a module function of the same package: without the roster composed there is
28	// nothing to mirror, and the injection is what holds the adapter until there is.
29	export const inject = ['components', 'agentPresets']
30	
31	/** Kind-specific detail of a `preset` component. */
32	export interface PresetComponentDetail {
33	  /** Trust recorded on the root the preset was discovered under. */
34	  readonly trust: PresetTrust
35	  /** Rows the mounted composition holds after `include` resolution. */
36	  readonly rows: number
37	}
38	
39	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types' {
40	  interface ComponentKindMap {
41	    /**
42	     * One standing preset composition currently mounted. A preset is in play
43	     * once its subtree is installed, which is what an agent joins; the roster
44	     * mounts one standing composition per preset, so two agents on the same
45	     * preset share one component.
46	     */
47	    'preset': PresetComponentDetail
48	  }
49	}
50	
51	const OWNER = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-presets'
52	
53	/**
54	 * Component id of one preset.
55	 * @param presetId - the preset's directory name.
56	 * @returns the stable id `preset:<id>`.
57	 */
58	export function presetComponentId(presetId: string): ComponentIdType {
59	  return ComponentId(`preset:${presetId}`)
60	}
61	
62	/**
63	 * One row's module specifier with a host path rewritten relative to the preset
64	 * directory, so two hosts that mounted the same composition under different
65	 * roots address identically. A package name or a specifier already relative to
66	 * the composition is canonical as authored.
67	 */
68	function portableName(rowName: string, presetDirectory: string): string {
69	  if (!isAbsolute(rowName)) return rowName
70	  return relative(presetDirectory, rowName).split(sep).join('/')
71	}
72	
73	/**
74	 * The composition rows of one mount, each `[id, name, config, disabled]`.
75	 *
76	 * A row's `config` is whatever the composition file supplied — a `!!js`
77	 * expression can evaluate to a value no JSON encoding preserves — so a config
78	 * that does not survive the lossless-JSON boundary contributes `null`, exactly
79	 * as an absent one does.
80	 */
81	function canonicalRows(mount: PresetMount): readonly ComponentCanonical[] {
82	  const directory = dirname(mount.path)
83	  return [...mount.tree.entries()].map(entry => [
84	    entry.options.id,
85	    portableName(entry.options.name, directory),
86	    snapshotJsonValue(entry.options.config as ComponentCanonical) ?? null,
87	    entry.options.disabled === true,
88	  ])
89	}
90	
91	/**
92	 * Content address of one `preset` component. The canonical value is
93	 * `[id, trust, rows]` over the composition after `include` resolution, so a
94	 * changed row moves the digest while the absolute root the preset was
95	 * discovered under stays outside it.
96	 * @param mount - the standing mount, whose tree holds the resolved rows.
97	 * @returns the digest over this kind and that canonical value.
98	 */
99	export function presetDigest(mount: PresetMount): ComponentDigest {
100	  return componentDigest('preset', [mount.presetId, mount.trust, canonicalRows(mount)])
101	}
102	
103	/** Describe one standing mount as a component. */
104	function describePreset(mount: PresetMount, digest: ComponentDigest, rows: number): ComponentDescriptor {
105	  return {
106	    id: presetComponentId(mount.presetId),
107	    kind: 'preset',
108	    digest,
109	    digestBasis: 'content',
110	    name: mount.presetId,
111	    description: `Agent preset "${mount.presetId}" of ${mount.trust} trust, composing ${String(rows)} row(s) that every agent joined to it runs on.`,
112	    owner: OWNER,
113	    // A `user` preset was authored locally, by a person or by an agent, and the
114	    // roster records no author; the honest reading of that trust is synthesized.
115	    provenance: mount.trust === 'user' ? 'synthesized' : 'curated',
116	    detail: { trust: mount.trust, rows },
117	  }
118	}
119	
120	/** One mirrored preset: the digest that produced it and the disposer that removes it. */
121	interface MirroredPreset {
122	  readonly digest: ComponentDigest
123	  readonly dispose: () => void
124	}
125	
126	/**
127	 * Mirror every standing preset mount and reconcile at each join.
128	 *
129	 * The roster publishes no mount notification, and its authoritative reading —
130	 * `livePresetMounts()` — prunes the record of every subtree whose fiber is
131	 * gone. The adapter therefore reconciles against that reading at the two edges
132	 * a session's composition changes at: an agent joining a standing mount
133	 * (`agent/created`, emitted after the factory's setup installed it) and a blank
134	 * session committing a different preset (`agent-preset/selected`). A mount torn
135	 * down with no later join stays listed until the next reconcile, which is

165	    mirrored.clear()

167	}

===== README.md =====
# @deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Mirrors every subagent provider registered with `ctx.subagents` into the component registry as an `agent-provider` component, following the seam's own `subagent/provider-added` and `subagent/provider-removed` events so the inventory tracks the live registry.

## Config

```yaml
- id: subagents
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
- id: components
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
- id: components-subagents
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents'
```

The adapter takes no configuration and requires both services.

## Contract

At mount the adapter registers one component per name in `ctx.subagents.list()`; afterwards it registers on `subagent/provider-added` and disposes on `subagent/provider-removed`, ignoring a duplicate addition or an unknown removal. Each component has id `agent-provider:<provider>`, kind `agent-provider`, `provenance: 'curated'`, no `invoke` pointer, and `detail: { provider }`. Disposing the adapter fiber removes every component it registered. `agentProviderComponentId(provider)` builds the id for consumers.

This adapter owns the `agent-provider` canonical value beside its `ComponentKindMap` declaration: `[provider]`, addressed by `agentProviderDigest(provider)` with `digestBasis: 'registration'`. The digest covers the registration and not the agent a provider starts, because the subagent seam exposes a provider name and its lifecycle edges, never the composition behind them.

## Model Experience

None, as the adapter registers component metadata only; the subagent tool owns every model-visible effect of the mirrored providers.

#### KV Cache effect

None; the adapter neither adds to nor changes any model request.

## Known Limitations and Deferred Work

- **No callable route** — the `subagent` tool is mounted per provider under a configurable `toolName` and takes no `provider` argument, and the subagent seam does not expose which tool instance is bound to a provider; the component carries no `invoke` pointer until the tools adapter mirrors tool-subagent instances with their provider binding.
- **Names only** — the component detail carries the provider name; provider capabilities (`outputSchema`, `depthLimit`, `toolFilter`, `persona`) are not mirrored until a consumer needs them. The digest inherits that limit: two providers of the same name registered by different plugins address identically, and a provider whose capabilities change without a re-registration keeps its digest.
- **Global registrations only** — the adapter mounts on a host context, so its components land in the global layer; a per-agent subagent registry would need the adapter mounted through that agent's scope.
- **Curated provenance for every provider** — providers are composed plugins today; a synthesized provider registered at runtime would need its producer to declare its own provenance and lineage.
===== README.zh.md =====
# @deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents

[English](README.md) | 中文

把注册在 `ctx.subagents` 中的每个 subagent 提供方镜像为组件注册表里的 `agent-provider` 组件，并跟随该 seam 自身的 `subagent/provider-added` 与 `subagent/provider-removed` 事件，使库存跟踪实时注册表。

## 配置

```yaml
- id: subagents
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
- id: components
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
- id: components-subagents
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-subagents'
```

该适配器不接受配置，并要求这两个服务同时存在。

## 约定

挂载时，适配器为 `ctx.subagents.list()` 中的每个名称注册一个组件；之后在 `subagent/provider-added` 时注册、在 `subagent/provider-removed` 时释放，忽略重复的添加或未知的移除。每个组件的 id 为 `agent-provider:<provider>`，类别为 `agent-provider`，`provenance: 'curated'`，不带 `invoke` 指针，`detail: { provider }`。释放适配器 fiber 会移除它注册的全部组件。`agentProviderComponentId(provider)` 为消费方构造该 id。

本适配器在自己的 `ComponentKindMap` 声明旁拥有 `agent-provider` 的规范值：`[provider]`，由 `agentProviderDigest(provider)` 寻址，`digestBasis: 'registration'`。摘要覆盖的是注册本身，而非提供方启动的 agent，因为 subagent seam 暴露的是提供方名称及其生命周期边，从不暴露其背后的组合。

## 模型体验

无，因为适配器只注册组件元数据；被镜像提供方的一切模型可见影响由 subagent 工具负责。

#### KV Cache 影响

无；适配器既不增加也不改变任何模型请求。

## 已知限制与暂缓事项

- **没有可调用路由** — `subagent` 工具按提供方各自挂载在可配置的 `toolName` 下且不接受 `provider` 参数，而 subagent seam 不暴露哪个工具实例绑定到哪个提供方；在工具适配器连同提供方绑定一起镜像 tool-subagent 实例之前，组件不携带 `invoke` 指针。
- **仅镜像名称** — 组件 detail 只携带提供方名称；提供方能力（`outputSchema`、`depthLimit`、`toolFilter`、`persona`）在有消费方需要之前不会被镜像。摘要继承这一限制：由不同插件注册的两个同名提供方地址相同，而未经重新注册就改变能力的提供方保持其摘要不变。
- **只做全局注册** — 适配器挂载在宿主上下文，因此它的组件落入全局层；按 agent 划分的 subagent 注册表需要该适配器通过那个 agent 的作用域挂载。
- **每个提供方都是人工筛选来源** — 如今提供方都是已组合的插件；运行时注册的合成提供方需要其生产方自行声明来源与谱系。

=== limitations ===

1 # Component registry 2 3 English | [中文](components.zh.md) 4 5 Types shared by the component registry and the adapters that mirror live seams into it. A component is one addressable unit of a composition: a plugin, or a plugin-provided member such as a tool, skill, subagent provider, workflow, MCP server, context provider, preset, or composition. The [component-registry Agent Note](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) owns the registry design and the [composition-manifest Agent Note](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-composition-manifest.md) owns content addressing and the scoped layers; this page records the exact fields from [`packages/components/components/src/types.ts`](../../packages/components/components/src/types.ts). 6 7 ## Descriptor 8 9 `ComponentId` is a [branded id](core.md#branded-ids) derived from the kind and the owning seam's stable name, never from mount order. Kinds are a merge-extensible map each producer package declares by declaration merging; the registry ships none. `ComponentDigestBasis` is `'content'` when a digest addresses the component's own bytes and `'registration'` when the component's model-visible text is a function of the assembly instead. 10 11 ```ts type-equiv 12 /** One addressable unit of a composition. */ 13 interface ComponentDescriptor { 14 /** Stable identity across compositions. */ 15 readonly id: ComponentId 16 /** Declared kind. */ 17 readonly kind: K 18 /** Content address of what this registration holds, computed by the producer that owns the kind. */ 19 readonly digest: ComponentDigest 20 /** What the digest covers. */ 21 readonly digestBasis: ComponentDigestBasis 22 /** Human-readable name. */ 23 readonly name: string 24 /** What the component does, stated for people and models. */ 25 readonly description: string 26 /** Package that produced the registration. */ 27 readonly owner: string 28 /** Curated by people or synthesized by an agent. */ 29 readonly provenance: ComponentProvenance 30 /** Component this one derived from, absent for roots. */ 31 readonly lineage?: ComponentId 32 /** Child components of a composition, absent for leaves. */ 33 readonly members?: readonly ComponentId[] 34 /** How a model reaches the component, absent for kinds without a callable route. */ 35 readonly invoke?: ComponentInvoke 36 /** Kind-specific detail. */ 37 readonly detail: ComponentDetail 38 } 39 ``` 40 41 ## Content address 42 43 `componentDigest(kind, canonical)` hashes the kind, a newline, and the JSON encoding of the producer's canonical value; `componentAddress(id, digest)` joins the id and digest as `id@digest`. Each producer owns its kind's canonical value beside its `ComponentKindMap` declaration, so the registry never switches on kind. 44 45 ```ts type-equiv 46 /** 47 * Lowercase 64-character SHA-256 hex over one component's kind and canonical 48 * value. Stored and compared at full length; truncating it for a card or a 49 * table is a presentation choice that never enters a log. 50 */ 51 type ComponentDigest = Branded<'ComponentDigest'> 52 ``` 53 54 ```ts type-equiv 55 /** 56 * JSON value a producer reduces its component to before hashing. Every field 57 * a digest must cover appears here; a value a registry computes per assembly — 58 * the viewing scope, the working directory, a wall clock, an absolute path, a 59 * discovery source or rank — must not, so two hosts that composed the same 60 * bytes address identically. 61 */ 62 type ComponentCanonical = 63 | null 64 | boolean 65 | number 66 | string 67 | readonly ComponentCanonical[] 68 | { readonly [key: string]: ComponentCanonical } 69 ``` 70 71 ## Scoped layers 72 73 A registration files into the layer of its calling context's [scope](scope.md); a read merges the global layer with the viewing scope's chain, the nearest layer winning a duplicate id. `ComponentLayer` is `'global'` when the winning registration sits in the context-global layer and `'agent'` when it sits anywhere on that agent's chain. 74 75 ```ts type-equiv 76 /** One descriptor read back through a viewing scope, carrying the layer its winning registration sits in. */ 77 interface ComponentView extends ComponentDescriptor { 78 /** Layer the winning registration under this id sits in for the reading scope. */ 79 readonly layer: ComponentLayer 80 } 81 ``` 82 83 ```ts type-equiv 84 /** Read options shared by every scope-aware registry read. */ 85 interface ComponentViewOptions { 86 /** Viewing scope (the calling agent); omitted reads the global layer alone. */ 87 readonly scope?: ScopeKey | undefined 88 } 89 ``` 90 91 ```ts type-equiv 92 /** List options: the viewing scope plus an optional kind filter. */ 93 interface ComponentListOptions extends ComponentViewOptions { 94 /** When given, only components of this kind. */ 95 readonly kind?: ComponentKind | undefined 96 } 97 ``` 98 99 ## Composition-time adapters 100 101 One adapter per seam, each mirroring what its own context's scope sees into that context's layer and owning its kind's canonical value beside its `ComponentKindMap` declaration. Mounted on a host row an adapter mirrors the global layer; mounted through an agent preset's composition it mirrors that agent's view into that agent's layer. 102 103 | Kind | Adapter | Canonical value | Basis | 104 |---|---|---|---| 105 | `tool` | [`components-tools`](../../packages/components/components-tools/README.md) | the model-facing `ToolSchema` as `ctx.tools.schemas(scope)` projects it | content | 106 | `prompt-section` | [`components-prompt`](../../packages/components/components-prompt/README.md) | `[name, order, complete === true, text]`, with `null` for a text the assembly evaluates | content, else registration | 107 | `preset` | [`components-presets`](../../packages/components/components-presets/README.md) | `[id, trust, rows]` over the composition after `include` resolution | content | 108 | `agent-provider` | [`components-subagents`](../../packages/components/components-subagents/README.md) | `[provider]` | registration | 109 110 Each adapter follows its seam's own change notification — `tools/change`, `system-prompt/change`, `agent/created` and `agent-preset/selected`, `subagent/provider-added` and `subagent/provider-removed` — so a registration disposed upstream disappears downstream, and disposing an adapter's fiber removes every component it registered. 111 112 ## The composition manifest 113 114 [`components-manifest`](../../packages/components/components-manifest/README.md) records what one agent had in play as a durable `composition/manifest` [session event](../persistence-catalog.md#compositionmanifest--log-only). On `agent/pre-step` it calls `next()`, recomputes `ctx.components.list({ scope: agent })`, and appends the manifest only when its `compositionSha256` differs from the last one in that session's log; deduplication is log-derived, so a stable composition records exactly one event and a resumed session re-emits nothing. 115 116 ```ts type-equiv 117 /** One component in play, as the manifest records it. */ 118 interface CompositionManifestEntry { 119 /** Stable component identity; with {@link digest} it forms the `id@digest` address. */ 120 readonly id: ComponentId 121 /** Content address of the generation in play. */ 122 readonly digest: ComponentDigest 123 /** The component's declared kind. */ 124 readonly kind: ComponentKind 125 /** Whether the digest covers the component's own bytes or only its registration. */ 126 readonly digestBasis: ComponentDigestBasis 127 /** Whether people curated the component or an agent synthesized it. */ 128 readonly provenance: ComponentProvenance 129 /** Component this generation derived from, absent for roots. */ 130 readonly lineage?: ComponentId 131 /** Registry layer the winning registration sat in for the recording agent. */ 132 readonly layer: ComponentLayer 133 } 134 ``` 135 136 ```ts type-equiv 137 /** The durable record of every component one agent had in play at one step. */ 138 interface CompositionManifest { 139 /** Payload version, so a later field addition is readable against a stated shape. */ 140 readonly version: typeof COMPOSITION_MANIFEST_VERSION 141 /** Every component in play, ordered by `id@digest` address. */ 142 readonly components: readonly CompositionManifestEntry[] 143 /** Lowercase SHA-256 hex over the ordered addresses joined by newlines. */ 144 readonly compositionSha256: string 145 } 146 ``` 147 148 ## Callable route 149 150 The invoke pointer names an existing tool and the arguments the component fixes; the model supplies the rest. The registry executes nothing. 151 152 ```ts type-equiv 153 /** The existing tool a model calls, with fixed arguments, to reach a component. */ 154 interface ComponentInvoke { 155 /** Registered tool name. */ 156 readonly tool: string 157 /** Arguments fixed by the component; the model supplies the rest. */ 158 readonly arguments?: Readonly> 159 } 160 ``` 161 162 163 164 165 166 ## Cordis API 167 168 Generated from source by `scripts/gen-cordis-catalog.ts` (verified fresh by `pnpm run verify-cordis-catalog` in doc-sync; regenerate with `pnpm run gen-cordis-catalog`) — this section is byte-identical in both language sides of the page.
